docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The purpose of this individual block diagram is to show the Timer/Scheduler subsystem for Team 101's Automatic Pet Food Dispenser. The subsystem uses a 5 V regulated power supply and a PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano as the primary microcontroller. The Timer/Scheduler uses a clock/timer circuit to generate a timing signal that is conditioned by an MCP6004-I/P operational amplifier before being read by the PIC through an ADC input. A push button provides a digital user input to the microcontroller. Connections to the other team subsystems are provided through the designated connectors. The Timer/Scheduler subsystem communicates with the other team subsystems to coordinate the scheduled dispensing of food.

docs.title: Automatic Pet Food Dispenser — Timer/Scheduler Subsystem
1. Project Overview
docs.text:
The purpose of this assignment is to compare commercially available components for the timer/scheduler subsystem of the automatic pet food dispenser. The selected components must support the intended operation of the circuit, interface with the PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano development board, and operate from the appropriate power supply.

The major components evaluated in this report are:

  • Timer IC
  • Operational amplifier/comparator stage
  • 5 V voltage regulator

Each category includes three commercial component candidates, their specifications, DigiKey product links, unit prices, advantages, disadvantages, and a final selection.

The microcontroller has already been selected for the project and is therefore not included as a candidate component.

Availability note: The prices and inventory quantities listed below are snapshots from DigiKey product listings when researched. Prices and stock levels may change.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The timer circuit provides a timing signal for the dispenser's control system. The signal is passed to the operational amplifier/comparator stage and then to the microcontroller for processing.

A 555 timer can be configured in monostable or astable operation, depending on the required timing behavior. However, its output is a pulse or switching waveform rather than a precision, continuously linear ramp. The final circuit configuration must therefore match the signal expected by the comparator and microcontroller.

docs.title: Candidate 1: Texas Instruments LM555CN/NOPB
docs.text:
• Manufacturer: Texas Instruments
  • Manufacturer part number: LM555CN/NOPB
  • Package: 8-pin PDIP
  • Unit price: Approximately $1.44
  • DigiKey product page: https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/texas-instruments/LM555CN-NOPB/6575
  • Datasheet: Available through the DigiKey product page
  • Product image: See the DigiKey product page.

Advantages - Established 555 timer architecture with extensive documentation. - Through-hole package is suitable for breadboard prototyping. - Supports timing and pulse-generation circuits. - Can operate from a 5 V supply.

Disadvantages - Generally consumes more supply current than CMOS 555 alternatives. - Requires external timing components to establish the desired interval. - Does not independently provide a precision linear ramp signal.

docs.title: Candidate 2: Texas Instruments TLC555CP
docs.text:
• Manufacturer: Texas Instruments
  • Manufacturer part number: TLC555CP
  • DigiKey part number: 296-1857-5-ND
  • Package: 8-pin PDIP
  • Unit price: Approximately $1.40
  • Stock snapshot: 13,095 units
  • DigiKey product page: https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/texas-instruments/TLC555CP/277502
  • Datasheet: Available through the DigiKey product page
  • Product image: See the DigiKey product page.

Advantages - CMOS timer design with low typical supply current. - Supports a 5 V supply. - Through-hole package is convenient for circuit prototyping. - Provides standard 555 timing functionality.

Disadvantages - Requires external resistors and capacitors to set the timing interval. - Has a higher unit cost than some bipolar 555 timer alternatives. - Its output waveform must be conditioned appropriately if the next stage requires a particular analog signal.

docs.title: Candidate 3: Texas Instruments NE555P
docs.text:
• Manufacturer: Texas Instruments
  • Manufacturer part number: NE555P
  • DigiKey part number: 296-NE555P-ND
  • Package: 8-pin PDIP
  • Unit price: Approximately $0.59
  • Stock snapshot: 33,422 units
  • DigiKey product page: https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/texas-instruments/NE555P/277057
  • Datasheet: Available through the DigiKey product page
  • Product image: See the DigiKey product page.

Advantages - Lower unit cost than the other timer candidates. - Established timer design with readily available documentation. - Through-hole package supports breadboard prototyping. - Supports supply voltages beginning at 4.5 V, including a 5 V supply.

Disadvantages - Typically draws more supply current than CMOS timer alternatives. - Requires external timing components. - Does not directly provide a precision linear ramp signal.

docs.title: Final Timer Selection: TLC555CP
docs.text:
The TLC555CP is selected because its CMOS design provides lower typical supply-current consumption while retaining the standard 555 timer functionality required for the timer subsystem. It also supports 5 V operation and uses a through-hole package suitable for prototyping.

The final circuit must use an appropriate timing configuration and external components to produce the signal needed by the following comparator stage.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The operational amplifier/comparator stage conditions or evaluates the timer signal before it reaches the PIC18F57Q43 microcontroller. Depending on the final circuit, this stage can amplify a signal, compare an input against a reference voltage, or condition the signal for the microcontroller's input.

The selected device must operate from the available supply voltage and provide an output compatible with the receiving circuit.

Design consideration: A general-purpose operational amplifier is not always interchangeable with a dedicated comparator. The final circuit must verify input common-mode range, output behavior, response time, and the required logic levels.

docs.title: Candidate 1: Microchip Technology MCP6004-I/P
docs.text:
• Manufacturer: Microchip Technology
  • Manufacturer part number: MCP6004-I/P
  • DigiKey part number: MCP6004-I/P-ND
  • Package: 14-pin PDIP
  • Amplifier channels: 4
  • Supply voltage range: 1.8 V to 6 V
  • Output: Rail-to-rail
  • Unit price: Approximately $0.59
  • Stock snapshot: 3,544 units
  • DigiKey product page: https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/microchip-technology/MCP6004-I-P/523060
  • Datasheet: Available through the DigiKey product page
  • Product image: See the DigiKey product page.

Advantages - Four amplifier channels are available in one IC. - Rail-to-rail output supports signal conditioning with a 5 V supply. - Low typical supply current. - Wide supply compatibility for low-voltage circuits. - Through-hole package is suitable for prototyping.

Disadvantages - Has a lower bandwidth than some higher-speed amplifier options. - Is a general-purpose operational amplifier rather than a dedicated comparator. - Output response and input voltage limits must be checked for comparator-style operation.

docs.title: Candidate 2: Texas Instruments LM358P
docs.text:
• Manufacturer: Texas Instruments
  • Manufacturer part number: LM358P
  • DigiKey part number: 296-1395-5-ND
  • Package: 8-pin PDIP
  • Amplifier channels: 2
  • Gain-bandwidth product: Approximately 700 kHz
  • Unit price: Approximately $0.33
  • Stock snapshot: 25,138 units
  • DigiKey product page: https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/texas-instruments/LM358P/277042
  • Datasheet: Available through the DigiKey product page
  • Product image: See the DigiKey product page.

Advantages - Dual amplifier channels in one package. - Supports low-voltage operation beginning at 3 V. - Established general-purpose amplifier architecture. - Through-hole package is suitable for breadboard prototyping. - Can be used for many basic signal-conditioning circuits.

Disadvantages - Output is not fully rail-to-rail. - Has fewer amplifier channels than the MCP6004-I/P and LM324N. - Input and output voltage limitations must be considered when interfacing with a 5 V microcontroller. - Is not a dedicated comparator.

docs.title: Candidate 3: Texas Instruments LM324N
docs.text:
• Manufacturer: Texas Instruments
  • Manufacturer part number: LM324N
  • DigiKey part number: 296-1391-5-ND
  • Package: 14-pin PDIP
  • Amplifier channels: 4
  • Gain-bandwidth product: Approximately 1.2 MHz
  • Unit price: Approximately $0.55

Advantages - Four amplifier channels in one IC. - Through-hole package is suitable for prototyping. - Supports a range of common signal-conditioning applications. - Provides multiple amplifier stages for future circuit expansion.

Disadvantages - Output is not rail-to-rail. - Input common-mode and output voltage limitations must be considered. - May require additional circuitry if the receiving microcontroller needs a specific logic-level signal. - Is a general-purpose operational amplifier rather than a dedicated comparator.

docs.title: Final Operational Amplifier Selection: MCP6004-I/P
docs.text:
The MCP6004-I/P is selected because it provides four amplifier channels, rail-to-rail output, low typical supply current, and operation from a 5 V supply. These characteristics make it a suitable candidate for low-voltage signal conditioning in the pet food dispenser's control circuit.

Before final implementation, the design must verify that the MCP6004-I/P's input and output behavior is appropriate for the comparator function. If fast, clean switching is required, a dedicated comparator should also be evaluated.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The voltage regulator supplies a regulated 5 V rail for the timer, signal-conditioning stage, and other circuit components that require this voltage. The regulator must support the system's total current demand and dissipate the heat generated during operation.

The block diagram specifies a 5 V regulator with a target current capability of 1.5 A. The current rating must be considered alongside the input voltage, thermal requirements, and actual load current.

docs.title: Candidate 1: STMicroelectronics L7805CV
docs.text:
• Manufacturer: STMicroelectronics
  • Manufacturer part number: L7805CV
  • Package: TO-220
  • Output voltage: 5 V
  • Maximum output current: Up to 1.5 A under appropriate electrical and thermal conditions
  • Unit price: Approximately $1.08
  • Stock snapshot: 89,629 units
  • DigiKey product page: https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/stmicroelectronics/L7805CV/585964
  • Datasheet: Available through the DigiKey product page
  • Product image: See the DigiKey product page.

Advantages - Fixed 5 V output. - Nominal current capability aligns with the 1.5 A regulator target. - TO-220 package supports heatsinking when necessary. - Includes thermal and short-circuit protection. - Established linear regulator architecture.

Disadvantages - Requires the input voltage to be sufficiently higher than 5 V. - Excess input voltage and load current generate heat. - May require a heatsink depending on operating conditions. - A linear regulator is generally less efficient than a suitable switching regulator.

docs.title: Candidate 2: onsemi MC7805CTG
docs.text:
• Manufacturer: onsemi
  • Manufacturer part number: MC7805CTG
  • Package: TO-220
  • Output voltage: 5 V
  • Maximum output current: 1 A
  • Unit price: Approximately $0.99
  • Stock snapshot: 43,687 units
  • DigiKey product page: https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/onsemi/MC7805CTG/919333
  • Datasheet: Available through the DigiKey product page
  • Product image: See the DigiKey product page.

Advantages - Fixed 5 V output. - Includes thermal and short-circuit protection. - Through-hole TO-220 package. - Suitable for lower-current 5 V circuits.

Disadvantages - Its 1 A output rating is below the block diagram's 1.5 A target. - Generates heat during linear regulation. - Requires adequate input voltage headroom. - Should not be selected if the design's required load current exceeds its rated capability.

docs.title: Candidate 3: Texas Instruments LM340AT-5.0/NOPB
docs.text:
• Manufacturer: Texas Instruments
  • Manufacturer part number: LM340AT-5.0/NOPB
  • Package: TO-220
  • Output voltage: 5 V
  • Unit price: Approximately $1.97
  • Stock snapshot: 13,152 units
  • DigiKey product page: https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/texas-instruments/LM340AT-5-0-NOPB/148173
  • Datasheet: Available through the DigiKey product page
  • Product image: See the DigiKey product page.

Advantages - Fixed 5 V output. - Through-hole package supports heatsinking. - Includes overcurrent and short-circuit protection. - Provides a documented linear-regulator solution for a 5 V rail.

Disadvantages - Has a higher unit cost than the other candidates listed. - Linear regulation can produce substantial heat at higher loads. - Input voltage must remain within the specified operating range. - Thermal performance must be checked at the expected load current.

Important: Verify the exact guaranteed output-current rating and thermal operating conditions in the datasheet before finalizing this candidate. Do not assume that every 5 V regulator in a TO-220 package can supply 1.5 A under all conditions.

docs.text: Feature L7805CV MC7805CTG LM340AT-5.0/NOPB Manufacturer STMicroelectronics onsemi Texas Instruments Output voltage 5 V 5 V 5 V Package TO-220 TO-220 TO-220 Nominal current capability Up to 1.5 A, subject to conditions 1 A Verify datasheet rating Thermal protection Yes Yes Yes Approximate unit price $1.08 $0.99 $1.97 DigiKey listing View View View

docs.title: Final Voltage Regulator Selection: L7805CV
docs.text:
The L7805CV is selected because its nominal output-current capability aligns with the 1.5 A target in the block diagram, and it provides a fixed 5 V output in a TO-220 package. Its thermal protection and established regulator design are useful for a prototype circuit.

The final design must verify the input voltage, total load current, regulator power dissipation, and heatsink requirements. A 1.5 A rating does not guarantee that the regulator can continuously deliver 1.5 A under every input-voltage and temperature condition.

docs.title: 5. Pin and Interface Table
docs.text:
The following table identifies the expected connections between the major components. Exact pin numbers must be taken from the selected components' datasheets and the final schematic.

Component Signal or Pin Function Connection / Purpose TLC555CP VCC Connect to the regulated 5 V supply TLC555CP GND Connect to circuit ground TLC555CP TRIG Receives the trigger signal required by the timing configuration TLC555CP THRES Monitors the timing capacitor voltage TLC555CP DISCH Discharges the timing capacitor as required by the circuit TLC555CP OUT Provides the timer output signal TLC555CP RESET Held at the appropriate logic level for normal operation TLC555CP CONT Connected as specified by the datasheet and circuit design MCP6004-I/P VDD Connect to the regulated 5 V supply MCP6004-I/P VSS Connect to circuit ground MCP6004-I/P Amplifier inputs Receive the timer signal and reference or feedback signals MCP6004-I/P Amplifier outputs Provide the conditioned signal to the next stage L7805CV Input Connect to the suitable unregulated DC input L7805CV Ground Connect to circuit ground L7805CV Output Supplies the regulated 5 V rail PIC18F57Q43 Power pins Connect to the required supply and ground connections PIC18F57Q43 ADC input Receives an analog signal only if its voltage is within the MCU's permitted input range PIC18F57Q43 Digital input Receives a compatible digital signal from the control circuitry

Note: The TLC555CP and MCP6004-I/P are both 8-pin and 14-pin PDIP devices, respectively. Use their datasheets to confirm the physical pin numbering and orientation. The PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano board's connector labels must be used when assigning actual board connections.

docs.title: 6. Final Component Selections
docs.text:
Major Component Selected Part Reason for Selection Timer IC TLC555CP CMOS timer with low typical supply current, 5 V compatibility, and a through-hole package Operational amplifier MCP6004-I/P Four amplifier channels, rail-to-rail output, and low-voltage operation 5 V regulator L7805CV Nominal 1.5 A capability and fixed 5 V output, subject to thermal and electrical conditions

These selections provide a starting point for the timer/scheduler subsystem. The final design must verify that the timer's waveform matches the required signal, that the amplifier stage operates correctly in its intended role, and that the regulator supports the complete system load.

docs.title: 7. Power Budget
docs.text:
A separate power budget should be completed after the remaining active components and their operating conditions are finalized. It should include:

  • The PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano board's current consumption.
  • The timer IC's supply current.
  • The operational amplifier's supply current.
  • The current required by all other active components.
  • The total current required from the 5 V rail.
  • A 25% safety margin.
  • Regulator input voltage and estimated power dissipation.
  • Thermal considerations and any heatsink requirements.
  • The selected external power source and its current rating.

The regulator must be selected based on the calculated system current, not solely on the nominal ratings of the individual components.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: The TLC555CP, MCP6004-I/P, and L7805CV are the recommended candidates for the timer, signal-conditioning, and 5 V regulation stages, respectively. Their suitability depends on the completed schematic, signal requirements, total power budget, and verification of all datasheet operating limits.
